After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said policymakers' focus should be on rising prices, markets are betting on a rate hike when The Fed meets September 16. The surprise 162,000 jobs added last month bolsters that expectation.

The Fed also monitors the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, which remains above the central bank's 2% annual target. This metric signals whether underlying price pressures are easing amid persistent supply shocks.
title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, as expected; core inflation was higher than estimated

Lynch discovered the molar in "immaculate condition" while surveying a creek for a habitat enhancement project supporting the threatened California red-legged frog.
The fossil was donated to Stanford University's Doerr School of Sustainability, where researchers plan to use carbon dating to determine its exact age and create a 3D scan.
This discovery helps researchers study Earth's past biodiversity, while Midpen officials noted the find illustrates the importance of protecting open spaces for endangered species.

summary: On Thursday, District Judge Cory Liu ruled TikTok violated Texas consumer protection law by misleading users about content filtering for minors and whether its 'Restricted Mode' feature shielded children from inappropriate material.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed the lawsuit in January 2025, alleging TikTok deceptively marketed its platform as safe for minors while regularly exposing children to inappropriate and explicit material.

According to the ruling, TikTok's 'Restricted Mode' 'did not work as advertised' and exposed minors to content the company said would be filtered out; internally, the platform classified harmful material as 'hard to find' rather than 'do not allow.'
The case will now proceed to trial where penalties and remedies will be determined, with proceedings expected to be scheduled next month, according to Paxton's office.

Paxton previously sued TikTok for violating the Securing Children Online Through Parental Empowerment Act and vowed to 'continue to go after' social media companies that expose children to inappropriate content or addictive features.
title: TikTok misled consumers about filtering content for minors, judge rules

summary: State Representative David Maloney is preparing a resolution urging President Donald Trump , Congress, and United States Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum to rename Lake Erie as "Lake Pennsylvania," arguing the Commonwealth deserves to name its only Great Lake.

Pennsylvania Sea Grant research shows roughly 74 percent of surveyed anglers reside in the state, traveling an average of 103 miles to reach Erie County's famed "Steelhead Alley." This tourism supports the region's economy across the Commonwealth.

Current naming honors Indigenous people, with "Erie" derived from the Iroquoian word "Erielhonan," meaning "long tail" and referring to the eastern cougar. The U.S. Board on Geographic Names generally discourages such changes, requiring compelling reasons.

While Trump previously proposed renaming New Mexico "New America" on social media, the White House has not announced official efforts for state-level lake renaming. Maloney's resolution faces significant bureaucratic hurdles under federal geographic naming standards.
title: State lawmaker calls on Trump to rename Lake Erie to ‘Lake Pennsylvania’

summary: On Thursday, researchers published findings in The Anatomical Record revealing that the spider-tailed horned viper's arachnid-like tail lure consists entirely of modified scales, not bone.

Scientists originally collected the specimen in 1968 but dismissed the tail as a tumor; only after a second individual was identified in 2003 did researchers recognize the appendage as a distinct evolutionary trait.
Field Museum researchers used X-ray computed tomography to scan the holotype, revealing normal vertebrae inside the tail and confirming the structure relies solely on keratin-based skin.

Lead author Georgios Georgalis noted the findings demonstrate how skeletal remains alone fail to reveal an animal's full morphology, limiting paleontologists' ability to reconstruct extinct species from fossils.

Museum collections remain vital for uncovering evolutionary secrets, according to senior author Sara Ruane, as these findings illustrate hidden diversity in snake evolution and unique survival adaptations.
title: Scientists Look Inside the ‘Spider’ Growing on the Tip of a Rare Viper’s Tail

Right-Leaning coverage emphasizes that 15 of 19 hijackers were Saudi nationals, alleged secrecy, and “betrayal,” portraying Strada as “courageously” going “off script” and casting Trump as families’ “last hope.” Both stress justice and alleged U.S. “protecting” of Saudi Arabia, but divide over Trump’s conduct and whether the episode signals health concerns or national-security failure.
Center coverage more cautiously uses “alleged” and adds practical details about the memorial’s closure, while all acknowledge the anniversary, victims, and disputed Saudi accountability.
summary: During Friday's 25th-anniversary ceremony at Ground Zero, 9/11 Families United chair Terry Strada urged President Donald Trump to hold Saudi Arabia accountable for the 2001 attacks, citing the kingdom's alleged role.
Families have long sought justice, noting that 15 of the 19 hijackers were Saudi nationals, though Saudi Arabia has consistently denied any state involvement or responsibility for the tragedy.
While Vice President Vance attended the New York ceremony, President Trump marked the anniversary at the Pentagon, where observers and media reports noted he appeared to doze off during the event.
Legal efforts continue, with a federal appeals panel in Manhattan scheduled to hear arguments next month regarding litigation that seeks to leverage newly unsealed evidence against Saudi Arabia.
title: 9/11 widow calls out government for protecting Saudis at 9/11 ceremony

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the handshake as a “show of unity,” portraying Giuliani’s unexpected civility positively while recalling his “Islamophobic broadsides”; right-leaning accounts emphasize that Mamdani attended “despite” calls to skip the memorial, recasting the same gesture as a “tense exchange,” “bitter war,” or “confrontation.” The pivotal divide is whether Giuliani’s prior claim that Mamdani’s presence “offends” him defines the encounter or is softened by reconciliation.
Center coverage stays closer to the observable handshake, noting inaudible remarks and treating prayer or encouragement as speculation.
All perspectives emphasize the Ground Zero setting, prior dispute, and brief handshake, reflecting wider divides over Islam, 9/11 memory, and partisan legitimacy.
summary: On Friday, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended the 25th annual 9/11 memorial ceremony at Ground Zero, where he exchanged a handshake with former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani.
Earlier this week, Giuliani unleashed an Islamophobic tirade during a Newsmax interview, demanding Mamdani skip the memorial and making baseless claims that he supports a Muslim anti-American plot.
Mamdani released more than 170,000 pages of city records on the governmental response to 9/11, accusing former leaders of lying to New Yorkers about toxic air safety at Ground Zero.
The video of the handshake drew more than 2.5 million views by Friday afternoon, sparking mixed reactions including criticism from right-wing activist Laura Loomer.

Politics largely took a backseat on Friday as families gathered to honor the nearly 3,000 lives lost 25 years ago, with the 9/11 Memorial ceremony featuring a seventh moment of silence for attack-related illnesses.
title: Mamdani and Giuliani shake hands at 9/11 commemoration

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Netanyahu’s brief UN visit through Gaza, the ICC warrant, and possible protests, using charged terms such as “war crimes” and “whirlwind” to stress accountability and escalating tension.

Right-Leaning coverage instead portrays him as defiant and obligated to attend—“there is no option”—while casting Mamdani’s arrest call as “political maneuvering” or “doing politics ,” and emphasizing that New York lacks authority to enforce the warrant.
Center coverage mediates these poles by noting the 24-hour itinerary, holiday and election timing, and competing claims.
All acknowledge the visit, warrant, arrest demand, and likely controversy, but diverge over accountability versus sovereignty and political resolve.
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will make a 24-hour trip to New York, arriving late Sept. 23 to address the General Assembly on Sept. 24 before returning to Israel that night.
Following Mayor Zohran Mamdani's arrest call over the war in Gaza, Ambassador Danny Danon said Netanyahu has "no option" but to attend the gathering despite the political pressure.

The International Criminal Court issued a warrant in November 2024 accusing Netanyahu of crimes against humanity, specifically alleging "starvation as a weapon of warfare" by restricting humanitarian aid; Israel denies the charges.
Danon warned that protests could "create more chaos" on New York streets during high-level meetings, adding, "I expect that there will be something like another show."

The gathering of leaders from 193 nations coincides with Jewish holidays and an Israeli election campaign, forcing Netanyahu to balance international diplomatic obligations with domestic political pressures.
title: Netanyahu will make a quick trip to speak at the UN after Mamdani urged his arrest, diplomat says

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Canada’s measure as punitive pressure responding to “rising violence,” “ sanctions ,” and settlement activity, while highlighting Israel’s accusation of “blatant interference” in its elections.

Right-Leaning coverage instead treats the ban as politically consequential, placing “illegal” in quotation marks and foregrounding warnings that it could fuel “attacks” or “intimidate” Canadian Jews; “Judea, Samaria” further signals a pro-Israel vocabulary.
Center coverage moderates the divide, presenting the action as a “turning point” toward a two-state solution.

All agree Canada coordinated with European allies to restrict settlement-linked, not all Israeli, goods, but their emphases reflect competing humanitarian, diplomatic, security, and geopolitical priorities.
summary: On Tuesday, Canada joined 11 other nations, including the U.K. and France, in pledging to ban trade in goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said Ottawa will implement restrictions "in the coming months."

The coalition condemned settler violence and settlement expansion, specifically citing the E1 development as actions "tantamount to the annexation of Palestinian land and forcible displacement of the Palestinian population." Twelve nations signed the statement framing these as illegal under international law.

Prime Minister Mark Carney noted the measures build on an advisory issued last month warning businesses of "legal, financial, and reputational risks associated with commercial activities linked to Israeli settlements." The government maintains a two-state solution remains fundamental to peace.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog called the announcement interference in Israel's election, while the foreign minister promised unspecified "counter measures" against participating nations. Israeli ambassador to Canada Iddo Moed warned the move undermines peace prospects and contributes to antisemitism.

Observers noted the ban is likely largely symbolic due to minimal trade volumes between Canada and Israeli settlements. Carney and other leaders plan to co-chair a meeting later this month at the United Nations General Assembly "to advance our efforts and pursue peace.
title: Canada Joins European Ban on Israeli Settlement Goods in Response to Rising Violence

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Iran as resisting “oppression,” “attacks,” and foreign interference, foregrounding Pezeshkian’s “won’t surrender” stance alongside Modi’s calls for “dialogue” and “peace.” Right-leaning coverage likewise portrays Iran as defying “bullying,” “arrogance,” and coercion, but broadens the stakes to sanctions, “Western financial hegemony,” local-currency trade , and Iran as a “strategic partner” in BRICS; it also highlights more sweeping conflict claims.
Center coverage de-emphasizes ideological language, stressing the Murmu meeting, BRICS diplomacy, and “dangerous” pressure.
All agree the visit occurred amid escalating tensions and that Iran rejected U.S.-Israeli pressure, reflecting wider divides over intervention, sovereignty, and global power.
summary: On Friday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrived in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, asserting Iran will not surrender to "bullying" and "arrogance" from the United States and Israel amid escalating West Asian hostilities.

Tensions escalated following a reported United States strike near a school in southern Iran that killed 168 children, prompting Pezeshkian to label United States and Israeli forces as "real militants" targeting civilian infrastructure.

Ahead of the BRICS summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi held wide-ranging discussions with Pezeshkian on West Asian stability and bilateral ties, where the Iranian President described "nice talks" on trade and technology cooperation.

Addressing the BRICS Business Forum, Pezeshkian pitched Iran's geography and energy resources as a strategic bridge for economic connectivity while advocating for stronger use of local currencies in BRICS trade.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi expressed confidence in India's leadership, calling the nation a "great emerging country" and confirming that BRICS members broadly support strengthening national currencies in intra-bloc trade.
title: Tehran won’t surrender to the U.S., Iranian President Pezeshkian says, as India's Modi urges dialogue and peace

bias: Center-Leaning coverage frames the Pentagon ’s roughly $5 billion proposal as provisional—“in talks,” reportedly funded through the Office of Strategic Capital, and not independently verified—while right-leaning coverage presents it more decisively as a planned or “record loan.” Both describe the goal as helping “shore up” the U.S. data-center supply chain, but the right adds an affirmative national-strategy frame, calling it a “striking sign” of AI’s industrial importance and emphasizing government-backed scale.
The pivotal divide is uncertainty versus commitment, alongside caution about an unsupported “record” label.
Both perspectives agree the financing signals AI infrastructure’s growing economic and geopolitical significance.
summary: The Pentagon is discussing a loan of about $5 billion to AI cloud startup Fluidstack to strengthen the U.S. data center supply chain.
The loan would be provided by the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital and used to boost supply chain and manufacturing capacity for data center components, not to build a new AI facility.
The Office of Strategic Capital has previously funded rare earth companies and drone companies, including Vulcan Elements and Unusual Machines.
title: Pentagon in talks to lend $5 billion to AI cloud startup Fluidstack, WSJ reports

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the lawsuit as part of a “growing list of allegations,” using “hurting” to stress LNG’s broader environmental and livelihood costs, while right-leaning coverage de-emphasizes that pattern and narrows attention to plaintiffs’ claims that dredging caused a sediment spill, “killed millions of oysters,” and reduced finfish catches.
The center presentation bridges these approaches through legal qualifiers such as “allegations,” though it retains “hurting” and details crabs, shrimp, and affected businesses.

The pivotal divide is whether the case signifies systemic corporate-environmental harm or a discrete disputed incident; all perspectives emphasize the lawsuit, alleged losses, and LNG development while lacking the company’s response or independent evidence.
summary: On July 30, a group of Louisiana commercial fishers filed a lawsuit in the 38th Judicial District Court against Venture Global, alleging that dredging for the $30 billion CP2 terminal caused a sediment spill destroying millions of oysters.

Venture Global acknowledged that a discharge of between 9,000 and 18,000 cubic yards of sediment traveled into a marsh bordering Calcasieu Lake last August, though the company maintains it has since worked with regulators on remediation.
Plaintiffs Anthony 'Tad' Theriot and David Sorrells lost 750,000 and 5.3 million oysters respectively, with Theriot estimating personal losses at over $450,000 and Sorrells at over $5 million.

The suit names dredging contractor Callan Marine Ltd., engineering contractor Providence Engineering and Environmental Group, and the Cameron Port, Harbor and Terminal District as defendants seeking damages for equipment losses and diminished catches.

Pending wastewater permitting, the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality is considering a discharge permit for the Calcasieu Ship Channel, while the Calcasieu Basin shrimp harvest dropped to half its 10-year average in 2024.
title: Lawsuit adds to allegations that Cameron Parish LNG terminals are hurting seafood industry

summary: On Thursday, Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico held a press conference in Dallas, calling on Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton to sue the Justice Department over the mishandling of Epstein files .
Talarico spoke at the Jeffrey Epstein Memorial Reading Room, a traveling exhibit featuring 3.5 million pages of records, alongside Epstein abuse survivors Annie Farmer and Sharlene Richard.
Critiquing Paxton for ignoring survivors, Talarico demanded the Attorney General use his power to 'sue the DOJ over the mishandling of these Epstein files,' targeting 2.5 million withheld files.

Paxton's campaign spokeswoman Madison Cercy responded by claiming Talarico's campaign infrastructure accepted over $11.5 million from Epstein's longtime associate Reid Hoffman, calling the accusations hypocritical.

Farmer stated she appreciated Talarico's efforts to hold the DOJ accountable, as the Senate race between Talarico and Paxton remains extremely close with candidates separated by only a few percentage points.
title: Epstein survivors back Talarico, urge Paxton to sue DOJ over redacted files

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the Pentagon commemoration as politicized, stressing that Hegseth “can’t read the room,” “exploiting tragedy,” and recycling allegedly false 9/11 war rationales; the pivotal divide is whether linking Iran to the attacks is historically misleading.

Center coverage de-emphasizes ideological judgment, describing a controversial speech and “harsh backlash.” Right-leaning coverage portrays the same linkage as a justified “continuation” of the “war on terror,” using “fiery,” “fight to win,” and “evil did not get the last word,” while emphasizing Iran’s nuclear threat and national resolve.
All perspectives acknowledge the ceremony, the Iran connection, and ensuing criticism, reflecting broader disputes over militarism, memory, and security.
summary: President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth honored victims at a Pentagon ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people.

Linking the 2001 tragedy to the current conflict with Iran, the defense chief vowed to "finish this fight" against what he described as the "world's most prolific state sponsor of terrorism" over the past six months.
These forces have destroyed air defenses and a navy, he said, warning that Washington remains "vigilant" against adversaries who continue to seek to "curb US power and kill American citizens."

The president added that officials are working to ensure the Islamic Republic will "never have a nuclear weapon," noting that the time since the initial incident has demonstrated the "power of the American spirit."
Public discourse continues to grapple with how that day shapes perceptions of Muslim Americans, as the rhetoric created broader, persistent tensions and a rise in prejudice.
title: Trump, Hegseth tie Iran war to 9/11 in speeches at Pentagon

summary: In a Quinnipiac University poll released Thursday, Democrats lead Republicans 49% to 38% for control of the House, a margin two months before the midterm elections.
Republicans gathered in Dallas as President Donald Trump unveiled a $5,000 plan for American adults, contingent on Republicans retaining control of both chambers of Congress in November.

Yet voters express broad dissatisfaction with Congress overall; just 21% approve of Democrats' performance while 26% approve of Republicans'. Tim Malloy noted Democrats are judged "more empathetic" regarding voter concerns.
Separately, 70% of voters oppose renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America, while six out of 10 disapprove of the White House ballroom construction the Supreme Court approved last week.

Voters remain divided on the ongoing Iran war strategy. Thirty-nine percent support keeping forces while negotiating, 30% favor withdrawal, and 22% want increased operations, reflecting deeper partisan splits.
title: Democrats top Republicans by 11 points for House control: Survey

King’s prayer at Michael Whatley’s GOP rally to questions of campaign judgment and accountability, while right-leaning coverage repeats the same stigmatizing label but treats the episode more as an unexpected personnel controversy than a broader party indictment.

Center coverage adds that convictions occurred in 1998 and 2010, involved children, and coincided with Democratic criticism of another alleged association, calling the contrast with a routine prayer “surprising.” All perspectives emphasize King, his record, Whatley’s event, and the prayer’s appeals to integrity and conservative grievances, reflecting wider disputes over partisan association and political responsibility.
summary: On August 28, Senate candidate Michael Whatley and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz attended a rally in New Bern, North Carolina, where twice-convicted sex offender Pastor Daimon King appeared prominently in the background.

Campaign spokesman DJ Griffin stated that Whatley did not know King, asserting the event "was NOT planned nor organized by the Whatley campaign nor did the campaign invite any of the guests." Griffin attributed the invitation to the Craven County Republican Party .
Democrats continue to hammer Whatley over his associations, spending more than $2.3 million on ads featuring a photo with West, a former state GOP committee chair and convicted sex offender.

Records show King was convicted 30 years ago of statutory rape and indecent liberties with a 15-year-old student, then pleaded guilty in 2010 to sex offenses with an underage relative, requiring lifetime sex offender registration.

With two months until the November elections, this Senate race could determine which party controls the chamber, making such revelations particularly damaging to Whatley's consolidation of party support.
title: Registered Sex Offender Led Opening Prayer at Michael Whatley Campaign Rally

bias: Coverage divides over emphasis: left-leaning accounts foreground the arrest and medical examiner’s homicide ruling, with one invoking “Black woman,” “hanging death,” and “red state” to add racial and political context.

Center coverage similarly stresses the police update, chronology, and formal classification, while right-leaning coverage spotlights a stark “murder investigation” and “hanging” behind a vacant home, de-emphasizing the arrest and examiner’s determination.

Across perspectives, Tasia Fortune is identified as a 29-year-old Black woman found near an abandoned home in Jackson, Mississippi; none specifies charges or identifies the suspect, underscoring how procedural, racial, and crime-focused frames shape interpretation.
summary: On Friday, Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney announced the arrest of a suspect in the death of Tasia Fortune after the state medical examiner officially ruled the case a homicide.
Fortune was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned house on the Road of Remembrance in early August; her parents disputed suicide claims and long suspected foul play.
During a Jackson City Council meeting, Councilman Kenneth Stokes read a letter from Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, stating, "I have no more answers from one day of this investigation."
Authorities arrested the suspect while walking along a city street, and Brackney said investigators expect to serve additional arrest warrants as the investigation continues.
The Jackson Police Department performed an autopsy four weeks ago but awaited the medical examiner's final determination; the homicide ruling now enables prosecution to proceed.
title: Jackson Police Arrest Man in Tasia Fortune Case After Homicide Ruling
